newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices ignore Japan, track U.S. up.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices ignore Japan, track U.S. up.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose on Wednesday, tracing the rise of U.S. treasuries and ignoring a rise in Japanese business confidence in the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey.
"The tankan report should be negative for yields but nothing happened," a dealer said.
At 0810 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.33, yielding 6.12 percent, up from Tuesday's 112.12.
The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, rose to 104.93, yielding 6.33 percent, from 104.65.
The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund was unchanged at 45 basis points. The 2007 gap to the bund was likewise static at 65 b.p.
The crown weakened slightly, to 3.8086 to the mark, from Tuesday's 3.8082. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
